column3: <what the change is>

column1: # library/ began as a byte-identical copy of the bootstrap's library at v0.0.162 (7ba8bd1d). The
# reference compiler is always run against ITS OWN library (SYSL_ORACLE_LIB, or the one installed
# beside it) and this compiler against this one, so after a change here the two compile against
# **The rule for an oracle sweep**: it may differ from the reference only in what reaches a module
# listed here. A sweep's disagreement is green when every disagreeing block, or every disagreeing
# symbol, reaches a listed module; anything else is a defect. With no rows the two libraries are the
# same bytes and every sweep must answer exactly as it does against the reference's library.

column3: new module, not in the reference's library: skip(why) -> never ends a test without a verdict (\u{3}, the reason, exit 0); outside the root module so it cannot collide with sysl.harness.skip

spare slots hold no value: storage is slot_storage, grow/push/extend/buf_with_capacity slot_place, pop/truncate/clear/remove slot_vacate; Buf is a reference handle over a boxed BufCore (assignment, parameter, capture and containment share one buffer; no zero value; elems a read-only property; copy() makes a second buffer)

six tests: set, pop, truncate/clear and remove let go at once; growth adds no count; buf_with_capacity keeps no fill; the invariant tests write a BufCore; ten share tests and two copy() tests; the zero-buffer test moved to the compiler (tests_brf_buf_reference.sysl)

slots are Option[T] filled with None, so a vacated slot owns nothing; Deque.elems and DequeCursor.elems private; Deque is a reference handle over a shared &DequeCore[T] (ring, head, count; head/count read-only properties), so every copy names one deque and deque() allocates

two tests: pop_front/pop_back let go of what they take out; clear lets go of every element and keeps no fill. Seven share tests: assignment (push_front through the copy), parameter, closure capture, nested deque, copied struct, growth through the other name, destructor waits for the last name

a child is started with posix_spawnp (macOS, glibc >= 2.29), not fork + execvp: fork cost grew with the parent heap (20 ms a test in a runner that had just compiled slate); the named variables are merged into the envp in the parent, and a PATH among them is searched as execvp searched it
one test: a variable named twice reaches the child once, with the second value

new module, not in the reference's library: Rational over BigInt in lowest terms (denominator positive, zero denominator traps, checked_of answers None), + - * / and negation, Eq/Ord/Hash, floor/ceil/trunc, n/d Display
new module file: from_real (exact), cmp_real/eq_real/lt_real/gt_real at the double's exact value (NaN unordered), to_real correctly rounded ties-to-even, subnormals included

30 tests: canonical form, checked_of, From (a bare literal reaching From[long] among two implementations), arithmetic, order, hashing, floor/ceil/trunc, exact real comparison, to_real ties, near-ties, subnormals and overflow
one test: BigInt.from(3) reaches From[long] rather than From[u64] (a bare integer literal prefers the signed widening)

Map is a reference: a one-field handle over &MapCore[K, V], which carries the table and both counts (a copy used to share the table and keep its own counts); every public method keeps its signature and delegates; cell/count/dead are read-only properties; map() allocates the core and still no table

ten tests: a put/grow/remove/clear through a second name, a by-value parameter, a closure capture, a map read out of a map, a copied holder struct and a walk all share; values are let go when the last name dies, and at the call on replace/remove
three tests: a Set shares through its Map (a second name, a by-value parameter, growth)
two tests, ignored until Buf is a handle: a Heap shares through its Buf (a second name, a by-value parameter)
add, remove and clear take the Set by value: a val-bound set is added to, the handle copy sharing the one map
push, pop and clear take the Heap by value: a val-bound heap is pushed into, the handle copy sharing the one Buf

new module, not in the reference's library: format_count(i128) -> int (a count saturated at int) and format_spec_of(width, prec, left) -> FormatSpec (C's reading of a negative count), which the compiler calls for an f"..." specifier whose width or precision is a hole
five tests: a count in range, saturation both ways, a negative width left-justifies, a negative precision is absent, the flag still left-justifies
